text:
mike_client: Hey, hitting a weird 400 from /v1/embeddings when I send a small batch. Works locally with one item but fails in our batch path. Error says 'expected array of strings, got string'.

mike_client: Example of what our service is POSTing (we use node fetch):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-v1","input":"[\"hello\",\"world\"]"}'
```

mike_client: Response body:
```json
{
  "error": "400",
  "message": "embeddings: expected array of strings, got string"
}
```

jess_support: Thanks — this is a classic double-encoding issue. The server expects input to be a JSON array (e.g. ["hello", "world"]) not a string containing JSON. Looks like something called JSON.stringify twice or wrapped the array into a string before sending.

jess_support: Can you share the raw request body object from your Node code (pre-JSON.stringify)? Also confirm your Content-Type header and whether any middleware is re-stringifying bodies.

mike_client: Pasted the snippet from our pipeline:
```js
// preprocessor returns an array of text items
const batch = preprocess(documents) // e.g. ["hello","world"]
const body = { model: 'embed-v1', input: JSON.stringify(batch) } // <-- oops
await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: {'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body: JSON.stringify(body) })
```

jess_support: Yup — that explains it. You're stringifying the array into a string and then stringifying the wrapper object, so server receives "input": "[\"hello\",\"world\"]". Fix: set input to the JS array (no JSON.stringify on batch) and then JSON.stringify the whole body once. Example: 
```js
const body = { model: 'embed-v1', input: batch }
await fetch(url, { headers: {'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body: JSON.stringify(body) })
```

sara_ml: Also flagging another pitfall we see a lot: some teams accidentally send nested arrays of tokens or numeric vectors (e.g. [[0.1,0.2,...]] or [["hello","world"]]) thinking the service will accept precomputed vectors or per-item token lists. Redwood embeddings API expects an array of strings (text) unless you intentionally are calling an endpoint that accepts vectors. If you do have precomputed vectors, check with support for the vector ingestion route — normal /embeddings expects text input.

jess_support: If you fixed the shape and still see mismatch errors downstream (e.g. your downstream dim-check fails), verify the model's embedding dimension (embed-v1 -> 1536 tokens) and confirm your downstream expects that size. We occasionally see confusion when a team mixes models (embed-small vs embed-large) and caches embeddings with different dims.

mike_client: Got it. I see the double JSON.stringify and also one preproc path that returned precomputed vectors by mistake. I'll flip the stringify, revert the preproc to return text, and re-run. Thanks! :raised_hands:

mike_client: One more: is there any SDK guard we can enable to catch this earlier?

jess_support: For Node + fetch, add a quick assert before sending: `if (!Array.isArray(body.input)) throw new Error('input must be array of strings')`. In our official SDKs we validate shapes before sending — migrating to the SDK prevents double-encode mistakes. If you want, paste the failing request id and we'll look at logs.

mike_client: Will do. Posting back if anything else pops up. Thanks.
